title.rendered: PR Tips for Nonprofits: Spreading Your Message Effectively

content.rendered:
In the nonprofit world, spreading your message effectively is crucial for garnering support, raising funds, and making an impact. Public relations (PR) plays a vital role in ensuring your organization’s message reaches the right audience. Here are some essential PR tips for nonprofits to help you spread your message effectively.

1. Define Your Mission and Goals Clearly

The foundation of any successful PR strategy is a clear and compelling mission statement. Your mission should succinctly convey what your organization stands for, what it aims to achieve, and why it matters. This clarity will help you craft messages that resonate with your audience and inspire action.

2. Understand Your Audience

Knowing your audience is key to effective communication. Identify who your supporters are, what they care about, and how they prefer to receive information. This understanding will allow you to tailor your messages to meet their interests and needs, ensuring greater engagement and support.

3. Leverage Storytelling

Storytelling is a powerful tool in the nonprofit sector. People are naturally drawn to stories that evoke emotion and highlight the human aspect of your work. Share compelling stories about the individuals or communities you’ve helped. Use quotes, photos, and videos to bring these stories to life, making your cause more relatable and impactful.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Media Strategy

A well-rounded media strategy is essential for spreading your message. Identify key media outlets, journalists, and influencers who are interested in your cause. Build relationships with them and provide them with timely, newsworthy content. Regular press releases, media pitches, and personal outreach can help secure media coverage and amplify your message.

5. Utilize Social Media Effectively

Social media is a cost-effective way to reach a broad audience. Develop a social media strategy that includes regular posting, engaging content, and interaction with followers. Use platforms like Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, and LinkedIn to share updates, stories, and events. Encourage your supporters to share your content to expand your reach organically.

6. Engage with Your Community

Building a strong relationship with your local community can significantly enhance your PR efforts. Participate in local events, collaborate with other organizations, and engage in community service. These activities not only increase your visibility but also demonstrate your commitment to the community, fostering trust and support.

7. Create High-Quality Content

High-quality content is crucial for capturing and maintaining your audience’s attention. Invest in creating professional-looking materials such as brochures, newsletters, blog posts, and videos. Ensure that your content is informative, visually appealing, and aligned with your brand’s voice and message.

8. Measure and Analyze Your Efforts

Regularly measuring and analyzing your PR efforts is essential for continuous improvement. Use analytics tools to track media coverage, social media engagement, website traffic, and other key metrics. This data will help you understand what’s working, what’s not, and how you can refine your strategies for better results.

9. Build Strong Relationships with Donors and Volunteers

Your donors and volunteers are your biggest advocates. Keep them informed and engaged by regularly communicating with them through newsletters, email updates, and personal outreach. Show appreciation for their support and highlight the impact of their contributions. Building strong, lasting relationships with your supporters can lead to increased loyalty and word-of-mouth promotion.

10. Stay Authentic and Transparent

In today’s world, authenticity and transparency are highly valued. Be honest about your successes and challenges, and communicate openly with your audience. Transparency builds trust and credibility, making people more likely to support your cause.

By implementing these PR tips, nonprofits can effectively spread their message, engage their audience, and make a greater impact. title.rendered: The Art of Crafting Unforgettable Experiences

content.rendered:
In a world saturated with brands and businesses vying for attention, creating unforgettable experiences is more crucial than ever. It’s not just about offering a product or service; it’s about leaving a lasting impression that resonates with your audience long after the initial interaction. But how do you craft such memorable experiences? Let’s delve into the art of making every touchpoint with your brand count.

1. Understand Your Audience

The foundation of any unforgettable experience lies in understanding your audience. Who are they? What are their needs, desires, and pain points? Conduct thorough market research, gather data, and create detailed customer personas. This insight allows you to tailor experiences that speak directly to your audience’s hearts and minds.

2. Create a Strong Narrative

Storytelling is a powerful tool in crafting memorable experiences. A compelling narrative can transform an ordinary product into an extraordinary experience. Your brand’s story should be authentic, relatable, and consistent across all channels. It should reflect your values, mission, and the unique value you bring to your customers.

3. Engage the Senses

Engaging multiple senses can enhance the memorability of an experience. Think about how you can incorporate visual, auditory, tactile, olfactory, and even gustatory elements into your interactions. This multi-sensory approach can create a deeper emotional connection and make the experience more immersive and memorable.

4. Personalization is Key

In today’s digital age, personalization is not just a nice-to-have; it’s expected. Utilize data and technology to personalize interactions and offerings. Whether it’s personalized email marketing, product recommendations, or bespoke customer service, making your audience feel seen and valued can significantly enhance their experience.

5. Surprise and Delight

Unexpected moments of delight can leave a lasting impression. This could be a handwritten thank-you note, an unexpected discount, or a special gift with purchase. These small gestures show that you go above and beyond for your customers, fostering loyalty and positive word-of-mouth.

6. Consistent Quality

Consistency is crucial in building trust and reliability. Ensure that every touchpoint, from your website and social media to in-store interactions, consistently delivers high quality. This reliability reinforces your brand’s reputation and keeps customers coming back.

7. Create a Community

Building a sense of community around your brand can elevate the customer experience. Foster connections between your customers through events, social media groups, or loyalty programs. This sense of belonging can turn customers into brand advocates who actively promote and support your business.

8. Feedback and Improvement

Continuously seek feedback and be open to making improvements. Listening to your customers’ experiences and acting on their feedback demonstrates that you value their opinions and are committed to providing the best possible experience.

9. Leverage Technology

Embrace the latest technology to enhance the customer experience. From augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) to artificial intelligence (AI) and chatbots, technology can offer innovative ways to engage and delight your audience.

10. Measure and Analyze

Finally, measure and analyze the success of your efforts. Use key performance indicators (KPIs) and analytics to track customer satisfaction, engagement, and loyalty. This data-driven approach allows you to refine your strategies and continually enhance the customer experience.

Conclusion

Crafting unforgettable experiences is both an art and a science. It requires a deep understanding of your audience, a commitment to quality, and a willingness to innovate and adapt. By focusing on these key elements, you can create memorable interactions that not only satisfy your customers but also turn them into lifelong brand advocates. At Bogues Group, we specialize in helping brands create these remarkable experiences. Visit our website to learn more about how we can support your journey to unforgettable customer interactions.

title.rendered: The Secrets to Memorable Event Planning

content.rendered:
Event planning is both an art and a science. It requires creativity, organization, and an acute attention to detail to create experiences that leave a lasting impression. Whether you’re planning a corporate conference, a wedding, or a community festival, the principles of memorable event planning remain the same. Here are the secrets to making your event unforgettable.

1. Define Clear Objectives

Before diving into the details, it’s crucial to understand the purpose of your event. What do you want to achieve? Whether it’s raising awareness, celebrating a milestone, or launching a product, clear objectives will guide your planning process and help you measure success.

2. Know Your Audience

Understanding your audience is key to planning an event that resonates. Tailor your event to their interests, preferences, and expectations. Conduct surveys or research to gather insights about what they would enjoy and find valuable.

3. Create a Detailed Plan

A comprehensive plan is the backbone of a successful event. Develop a timeline that includes all the tasks leading up to the event, from securing a venue to sending out invitations. Use project management tools to keep track of progress and ensure nothing falls through the cracks.

4. Choose the Right Venue

The venue sets the tone for your event. Consider factors like location, capacity, and ambiance. Make sure the venue aligns with your event’s theme and can accommodate all your needs, including AV equipment, catering, and accessibility.

5. Focus on Guest Experience

From the moment attendees arrive to the time they leave, every touchpoint should enhance their experience. Consider elements like signage, registration processes, and seating arrangements. Personal touches, like welcome gifts or personalized name tags, can make guests feel valued and appreciated.

6. Engage Your Audience

Interactive elements can make your event more engaging and memorable. Incorporate activities that encourage participation, such as live polls, Q&A sessions, or hands-on workshops. Social media integration can also enhance engagement, allowing attendees to share their experiences in real time.

7. Pay Attention to Details

The small details can make a big difference in how your event is perceived. From the décor and lighting to the music and menu, every element should reflect your event’s theme and objectives. Attention to detail shows your guests that you care and adds a touch of professionalism.

8. Have a Contingency Plan

Even the best-laid plans can encounter unexpected challenges. Prepare for potential issues by having a contingency plan in place. Whether it’s bad weather, technical difficulties, or last-minute cancellations, being prepared can help you handle problems smoothly and keep your event on track.

9. Evaluate and Follow Up

After the event, take time to evaluate its success. Gather feedback from attendees, review your objectives, and analyze what worked well and what could be improved. Follow up with thank-you notes to attendees, sponsors, and vendors, and share highlights from the event on social media or through a post-event report.

10. Partner with Professionals

If the scope of your event is beyond your expertise, consider partnering with professional event planners. Their experience and resources can help you execute your vision flawlessly and take the stress out of the planning process.

Conclusion

Memorable event planning requires a blend of creativity, meticulous planning, and a focus on guest experience. By defining clear objectives, knowing your audience, and paying attention to details, you can create events that leave a lasting impression. Remember to evaluate your efforts and continuously improve, ensuring each event is better than the last. For more tips and professional event planning services, visit Bogues Group. title.rendered: The Future of Marketing: 10 Trends to Watch

content.rendered:
As we navigate through an ever-evolving digital landscape, the future of marketing stands on the brink of a new dawn, driven by innovation, technology, and an ever-deepening understanding of consumer behavior. 

Here are key trends poised to shape the marketing world:

1. Personalization at Scale: The era of one-size-fits-all marketing is behind us. Advances in AI and machine learning enable marketers to tailor content, products, and experiences to individual preferences at an unprecedented scale. Salesforce reports that 52% of consumers expect offers to always be personalized, highlighting the demand for bespoke experiences.

2. Conversational Marketing and Chatbots: The rise of messaging apps and AI-driven chatbots facilitates real-time, personalized engagement with consumers. According to a survey by Drift, 41% of consumers enjoy quick responses to questions as a major benefit of chatbots, making conversational marketing a key player in future strategies.

3. Sustainability and Ethical Marketing: Consumers are increasingly aligning their purchases with their values. NielsenIQ reveals that 73% of global consumers are willing to change their consumption habits to reduce their environmental impact. Brands that prioritize sustainability and ethical practices in their marketing narratives will resonate more with this growing consumer base.

4. Augmented Reality (AR) Experiences: AR offers immersive experiences that bridge the gap between digital and physical worlds. From virtual try-ons to interactive ads, AR can enhance the consumer journey in engaging ways. Snap Inc. reports that their AR features influence over $500 billion in consumer purchases, underscoring AR’s potential impact.

5. Influencer Marketing Evolution: The influencer marketing realm is expanding beyond celebrities to include micro-influencers and brand advocates who wield significant influence within niche communities. A HubSpot study shows that 89% of marketers find ROI from influencer marketing comparable to or better than other marketing channels, highlighting its enduring value.

6. Voice Search Optimization: With the increasing use of digital assistants, optimizing for voice search is becoming crucial. ComScore predicts that by 2022, 55% of households will own smart speaker devices, making voice search optimization a critical aspect of SEO strategies.

7. Interactive Content: As audiences crave more engaging and immersive content, interactive formats like quizzes, polls, and 360-degree videos are gaining traction. According to DemandGen, interactive content is twice as effective at engaging audiences compared to static content, signaling its growing importance.

8. Privacy-First Marketing: With rising concerns about data privacy and changes in regulations, marketers must adopt privacy-first strategies. Transparency and respect for user privacy can build trust and foster stronger customer relationships.

9. Blockchain in Marketing: Blockchain technology offers new ways to ensure transparency, security, and trust in marketing practices, from verifying the authenticity of products to managing secure transactions.

10. AI-Driven Content Creation: AI’s role in content creation is expanding, from generating data-driven insights for content optimization to creating personalized content experiences. Gartner predicts that by 2023, AI will enable effective decision making in over 33% of large organizations.

As these trends unfold, the future of marketing promises a landscape where technology, ethics, and creativity converge to create more meaningful and effective engagements with consumers. Marketers who stay ahead of these trends and adapt their strategies accordingly will thrive in the dynamic world of tomorrow. Find these tips helpful? title.rendered: Celebrating Women in Business: Strategies for Success

content.rendered:
In the dynamic landscape of modern entrepreneurship, women in business are not just participating; they are leading the charge. As we celebrate the strides made by women entrepreneurs, it’s crucial to recognize the unique challenges they face and the strategies that drive their success.

Embrace Your Unique Perspective

Women bring different life experiences and perspectives to the business world, which can be leveraged as a powerful tool for innovation. Use your unique viewpoint to identify gaps in the market, understand diverse customer needs, and create solutions that stand out. Authenticity resonates with consumers, and by being true to yourself, you’ll foster a brand that is both genuine and relatable.

Build a Supportive Network

A robust network is invaluable. From mentors who can offer guidance to peers who can share insights, building relationships is key. Networking isn’t just about exchanging business cards; it’s about creating meaningful connections that can open doors to new opportunities. Engage with professional groups, attend industry events, and don’t be afraid to reach out to those you admire.

Focus on Financial Literacy

Financial acumen is critical. Understanding the numbers behind your business allows you to make informed decisions, secure funding, and maintain profitability. Invest time in learning about financial management or partner with experts who can guide you. Knowledge is power, especially when it comes to managing your business’s financial health.

Prioritize Work-Life Harmony

The pursuit of work-life balance is often a misnomer; it’s more about harmony. As a woman in business, it’s essential to integrate personal well-being with professional ambitions. Set boundaries, know when to delegate, and remember that taking time for self-care isn’t a luxury—it’s a necessity for sustained success.

Utilize Technology and Tools

In today’s digital age, technology can be a great equalizer. Use digital tools to automate tasks, streamline processes, and increase productivity. Whether it’s managing customer relationships, optimizing social media, or tracking your finances, there’s a plethora of apps and software designed to make your life easier.

Cultivate Resilience and Adaptability

The path of entrepreneurship is rarely linear. It requires the ability to pivot in response to market changes, learn from setbacks, and persist despite obstacles. Resilience is about bouncing back stronger, and adaptability is about embracing change as an opportunity for growth.

Champion Diversity and Inclusion

Diversity drives innovation. As a woman in business, championing diversity and inclusion isn’t just a moral imperative; it’s a business strategy. Encourage diverse ideas, foster an inclusive environment, and tap into the collective strength of varied experiences and backgrounds.

Celebrate Every Milestone

Finally, take the time to celebrate your achievements, no matter how small. Each milestone is a testament to your hard work and dedication. Celebrating progress keeps you motivated and sets the stage for future success.

As we honor the contributions of women in business, let’s continue to support, empower, and inspire one another. The success of women entrepreneurs is not just an individual triumph but a collective advancement for the business community.

At Bogues Group, we’re committed to providing the tools, strategies, and support that women in business need to thrive. Let’s continue to break barriers and build futures together.

title.rendered: The Disparity: The Rise of CBD as Marijuana Incarceration Persists

content.rendered:
As CBD gains popularity as a wellness drug, it is crucial to address the ongoing disparity in marijuana-related incarcerations. While CBD is celebrated for its health benefits, a disproportionate number of BIPOC individuals continue to face imprisonment for marijuana offenses. This stark contrast raises concerns about social justice and equal treatment under the law.

In the United States, with almost 2 million people incarcerated across various facilities, the living conditions are often substandard, with extreme temperatures, violence, and unsafe environments. The traumatic experiences in these institutions significantly impact mental health, leading to high rates of PTSD among inmates. Studies have shown that up to 48% of incarcerated individuals have PTSD, which is over five times higher than the general population. Symptoms of PTSD commonly reported include avoidance, nightmares, hypervigilance, and emotional numbness.

The Failed War on Drugs and Soaring Incarceration Rates:

Decades of the failed war on drugs have resulted in alarming incarceration rates in the United States. Harsh penalties for drug offenses introduced during President Nixon’s war on drugs in the 1970s have led to a sevenfold increase in the incarcerated population, with one out of five individuals serving time for a drug offense.

The Disproportionate Impact on BIPOC Communities:

Communities of color have disproportionately suffered the consequences of these punitive drug policies. Racial discrimination is deeply ingrained in drug enforcement, with laws historically targeting Chinese immigrants, Black Americans, and Mexican migrants. Today, despite representing a minority of the population, Black and Latino Americans make up two-thirds of the prison population, primarily due to discriminatory enforcement of marijuana laws.

Changing State Laws and the Federal Crossroads:

Several states have embraced progressive marijuana legislation, decriminalizing and legalizing its use for both medical and recreational purposes. These state-level reforms have demonstrated positive outcomes in public health and the economy while maintaining public safety. It is now time for the federal government to learn from these state experiments and consider the path towards nationwide marijuana legalization.

Seeking Smarter and Fairer Criminal Justice Policy:

In the face of a glaring disparity, it is time for comprehensive criminal justice reform. By adopting smarter and fairer drug policies, the United States can work towards a system that promotes equity, public health, and equal treatment for all citizens.

While CBD gains popularity as a wellness drug, the disproportionate incarceration rates for marijuana offenses persist, particularly affecting BIPOC communities. Addressing this disparity is essential in the pursuit of social justice. The nation can move closer to a fairer and more equitable future by reevaluating drug policies and embracing comprehensive criminal justice reform.

title.rendered: National Minority Health Awareness Month

content.rendered:
Blog by Lexi Lutz

Our minds and bodies are intrinsically connected, so it should come as no surprise that our mental health can have significant effects on physical health. Good mental health can positively affect your physical health. Conversely, poor mental health can negatively affect your physical health.  Challenges in accessing mental health care exist for everyone, which include cost, lack of insurance coverage, and stigma. Unfortunately, minority groups face unique challenges in accessing mental health care due to factors that are unique to minority groups, such as inability to find providers from one’s own racial or ethnic group, and stress caused by experiencing/witnessing racial discrimination or racial violence.

For some people, particularly in some minority groups, it is important to see a mental health care provider who is from their own racial or ethnic group. This can help to ensure that the provider can understands and empathize with the patient’s cultural background and experiences. It can be difficult, however, to find providers who are from minority groups in certain locations, especially in rural areas.

Additionally, a person who experiences or witnesses racial discrimination or racial violence can create mental health problems due to stress or trauma created by such situations. Minority groups are more likely to experience and witness racial discrimination or racial violence, putting minorities at higher risk for mental health issues caused by these unfortunate experiences.

Mental health care challenges are not exclusive to minority groups; however, minorities do face risk of unique factors that could create challenges to receiving mental health care that tend to effect minority groups more so than non-minorities.  Support organizations that are working to improve access to mental health care for people from racial and ethnic minority groups include: National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) (https://www.nami.org/) and Mental Health America; (https://www.mentalhealthamerica.net/).

title.rendered: 5 Ways We Can Make the Workplace Better for Black Women Starting This Minority Mental Health Awareness Month

content.rendered:
Going to work should not bring on a sense of dread or fright, but for so many employees, that is a reality. On a daily basis, employees are silenced, overworked and belittled, which makes for a hostile work environment, but that does not have to be the case. We can create and enact policies that foster an inclusive work environment.

I remember being laughed at by an older white male CEO who basically said a millennial Black woman wasn’t a CEO or business owner and the role was regulated for Fortune 500 executives. I felt so defeated but decided to research and found that the workforce was made up of almost 50% women yet only 25% were in leadership and less than 10% in C-Suite with just 2% being women of color by his standards. I already thought his definition was antiquated but I knew we needed a greater shift – a cultural shift for sure so I created The C-Suite Is Calling Members Club. Our group aims to see an increase in female leadership in the next 10 years by creating a more inclusive environment. Here are 5 ways to create a more inclusive environment:

  1. Establish clear boundaries for work hours to prevent burnout
  2. Set Policies that promote Flexibility for Caregivers & Parents
  3. Cultivate a workplace that is inclusive and empowers/ supports women
  4. Be open to being a mentor
  5. Having Men allies/ supporters

Join our Members Club and receive our bi-weekly newsletter for free Resources, access to mentors and more: https://boguesgroup.com/c-suite-club/

title.rendered: Starting A Business Venture

content.rendered:
Starting a new business venture is an exciting journey filled with challenges and opportunities. Aspiring entrepreneurs often find themselves brimming with innovative ideas, passion, and a burning desire to make their mark in the business world. However, one crucial aspect that can significantly impact the success of these budding entrepreneurs is the strategic utilization of resources. In this digital age there are a plethora of free and or low costs resources to help your business build a foundation for success.

In the dynamic landscape of entrepreneurship, resources come in various forms – financial capital, time, knowledge, and human capital. Recognizing the need to harness these resources effectively can make the difference between a thriving startup and one that struggles to take off.

First and foremost, financial capital plays a pivotal role in getting a new business off the ground. Entrepreneurs need to allocate resources wisely, ensuring that funds are directed towards critical areas such as product development, marketing, and operational infrastructure. While bootstrapping is a commendable approach, seeking external funding or exploring partnerships can provide the necessary financial boost for growth.

Time is another invaluable resource that new entrepreneurs must manage judiciously. The early stages of a startup demand intense commitment and dedication. Prioritizing tasks, setting realistic goals, and staying focused on the long-term vision can help entrepreneurs make the most of their time. Effective time management also involves learning to delegate tasks and build a reliable team.

Knowledge is power, especially in the ever-evolving business landscape. Entrepreneurs need to continuously educate themselves about market trends, industry best practices, and the competitive landscape. Investing time and effort in acquiring knowledge can lead to informed decision-making and a competitive edge in the market.

Human capital, represented by the skills and expertise of the team, is a critical resource that should not be underestimated. Building a diverse and talented team is essential for tackling the multifaceted challenges that come with entrepreneurship. Collaborating with individuals who bring different strengths to the table enhances the overall capabilities of the startup.

In conclusion, the need for entrepreneurs to use resources wisely cannot be overstated. Whether it’s financial capital, time, knowledge, or human capital, strategic utilization can pave the way for sustainable growth and success. By recognizing the importance of resource management, aspiring entrepreneurs can navigate the complexities of the business world with confidence and resilience. After all, the journey of entrepreneurship is not just about having great ideas; it’s about turning those ideas into reality through effective resource allocation and management. title.rendered: Best Jobs for Entrepreneurs

content.rendered:
1. Try starting a freelance consulting firm: Utilize your expertise in a specific field and offer consulting services to businesses or individuals.
  2. Get involved in e-commerce: Start an online store or marketplace, selling products or services to a global customer base.
  3. Become a content creator: Build a platform, such as a blog, YouTube channel, or podcast, and generate income through advertisements, sponsorships, or product endorsements.
  4. Consider event planning: Organize and manage events, such as conferences, weddings, or trade shows, catering to the specific needs and preferences of clients.
  5. Create an online course: Share your expertise in a specific subject by creating and selling online courses to learners worldwide.
  6. Get involved in real estate: Help individuals buy, sell, or rent properties, earning commissions based on successful transactions.

You can even enter the personal health & wellness space!

  1. Health and wellness coach: Guide individuals in achieving their health and wellness goals through personalized coaching and support.
  2. Personal trainer/fitness coach: Provide personalized fitness training and coaching services to clients, either in-person or online.

Remember that entrepreneurship requires dedication, creativity, and adapting to challenges. Choosing a job that aligns with your skills, interests, and passions is important.

title.rendered: The People Pleaser

content.rendered:
We’re excited to launch our guest blog series with none other than Lawrese Brown, the Founder of C-Track Training. Lawrese has expertly navigated spaces previously unavailable or inaccessible to marginalized communities. It is my pleasure to feature her in this month’s blog as we reflect on the gems she dropped during the May installment of the C-Suite Is Calling: Coffee & Conversations. To close out Mental Health Awareness month, Lawrese has penned a blog that I know you’ll need to bookmark and reference regularly.
 
Sign up for the next Coffee & Conversations here: https://bit.ly/BGjunecoffeeconvo

 

We all know one, and many of us are one.
 
We are the colleagues and friends that measure our success by how ‘good’ we are to others, so we: 

  • Say ‘we should all improve’ instead of ‘I need you to improve’ when asking others to change their behaviors so they don’t feel called out.
  • Over-emphasize that both sides have good points when resolving conflict among others so that no one feels offended.
  • Say ‘yes’ without hesitation to any request for our time so that everyone feels supported.

These ‘good’ behaviors lead to burnout because:

  • Our indirect language means people aren’t held accountable for their behaviors, and those behaviors never change.
  • Continuously playing politics means we don’t draw boundaries, give consequences or take a stand on tough topics.
  • Extending yourself to support others, but not asking for help from others leads to imbalance, draining relationships.

Being a people pleaser means you are welcoming, receptive, and supportive of others needs, but indecisive and self-sacrificing towards your own.

Preventing burnout means developing the skills needed to build balanced relationships, including:

  • Being more direct about your needs, wants, and goals without lingering too long on how they could be received.
  • Taking a pause to consider how fulfilling a request will impact you rather than focusing exclusively on how much the other person will appreciate you if you do it.
  • Sitting with tension during conflict without rushing to play peacemaker so that you can discern when to accommodate vs. when to push for needs to be acknowledged and met.
     

As the saying goes, how can you be good to others if you aren’t good to yourself? The latter is the key to preventing burnout and improving mental health.
 
As a work-coach, my specialty is supporting people pleasers in developing the self-awareness and self-leadership skills that enable them to build reciprocal relationships, to directly communicate expectations and needs, and to move away from waiting for others permission/validation to standing in your personal authority. title.rendered: The Importance of DEI in Marketing

content.rendered:
Are you tired of feeling excluded by products and events that don’t seem to cater to your interests or needs? Maybe you’ve seen a product you like, but it’s hard to visualize how it could fit into your daily life. It’s frustrating to see something that appeals to you but not see yourself represented. Marketing and PR play a vital role in promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) initiatives, especially when it comes to increasing representation and creating an inclusive workplace culture for women. In the marketing industry, women, especially women of color, have historically faced numerous challenges, including a lack of opportunities for career advancement and leadership roles.

However, with the increasing adoption of DEI initiatives, there has been a positive impact on the lives of women in the marketing business. DEI initiatives in marketing foster a more equitable and diverse industry where women can bring their unique perspectives and experiences to the table. 

Here are some reasons why it’s essential to prioritize DEI in marketing roles: 

Representation Matters

Having women in marketing roles helps in creating an inclusive and diverse industry. When women are better represented in marketing, it leads to more creativity and innovation, and the industry can better understand and cater to diverse audiences.

Positive Impact on Brand Reputation

Marketing is all about perception; a company with a diverse workforce is seen as progressive and inclusive. Organizations that prioritize DEI initiatives create a positive reputation, and it helps them attract and retain customers and employees.

More Significant Insights into Consumer Needs

Marketing is all about understanding the customer’s needs, and having women of color in marketing roles can help companies understand diverse perspectives and needs. This understanding leads to more accurate messaging and better customer engagement.

Better Decision Making

Diverse teams lead to better decision-making because they bring diverse perspectives and experiences. Women in marketing bring unique insights and skills that help to make more informed and thoughtful decisions, leading to better outcomes for the organization.

Diversity, equity, and inclusion are essential for any industry, and marketing is no exception. Women bring unique perspectives and experiences to marketing roles, which can enhance brand reputation, increase customer engagement, and lead to better decision-making. Therefore, it is crucial to support and promote DEI initiatives in marketing to create a more equitable and inclusive industry.

The Bogues Group is proud to be founded and run by two amazing Black women who have been friends since high school. Not only are we putting forward the needs of women in business, but we are highlighting the importance of Black women in business spaces. While all women are still represented at a lower rate than men in the C-suite, white women are 4.5% more likely to hold a leadership position than Black women. The Bogues Group aims to provide the resources and support necessary to build up Black women in business, which is why we launched The C-Suite is Calling, a call to action for everyone to advocate for female leadership in the workforce. The initiative includes multiple opportunities for engagement. Each touchpoint creates a space for continuous growth, collaboration and innovation through thought leadership panels and networking events, monthly coffee and conversations, membership community, and more. We hope you will join us in creating a better world where all women can succeed and thrive in and out of the workplace. Learn about sponsorship and partnership opportunities here.

The Bogues Group is proud to be founded and run by two amazing Black women who have been friends since high school. Not only are we putting forward the needs of women in business, but we are highlighting the importance of Black women in business spaces. While all women are still represented at a lower rate than men in the C-suite, white women are 4.5% more likely to hold a leadership position than Black women. The Bogues Group aims to provide the resources and support necessary to build up Black women in business, which is why we launched The C-Suite is Calling, a call to action for everyone to advocate for female leadership in the workforce. The initiative includes multiple opportunities for engagement. Each touchpoint creates a space for continuous growth, collaboration and innovation through thought leadership panels and networking events, monthly coffee and conversations, membership community, and more. We hope you will join us in creating a better world where all women can succeed and thrive in and out of the workplace. Learn about sponsorship and partnership opportunities here.

title.rendered: The Importance of DEI in Marketing
What’s Happening to Female Leadership?

content.rendered:
Gone are the days when women blended into the background and minded their place. Nowadays, they are empowered and emboldened to speak their mind and give pushback when necessary, something more prominent in today’s workplace. The biggest challenge many companies are encountering is keeping a hold on their female leadership – an already underrepresented dynamic. The pandemic opened the eyes of many, showing that staying in a toxic work environment is not worth the stress or sacrifice on one’s well-being. Companies are seeing female workers leaving in droves, a vast majority being female leadership. So what is the issue? What is causing this, and what can companies do to lower this troubling statistic? 

Female Leadership is Overwork, Undervalued

Women are often seen as more emotional than men. Women often connect with others on an emotional level, meaning female leaders are usually the ones who support and advocate for employee well-being. This results in higher retention rates and employee morale; however, they are not always rewarded or recognized for this effort. This is often something that upper management doesn’t pay any mind to since they only worry about the bottom line. Doing work that is not acknowledged while constantly being overworked can make one feel unappreciated. This could be why many female leaders leave to find a place where they are valued, celebrated, and supported in their job. 

Motherhood

The Motherhood Penalty is nothing made of fiction. It is very much real and frequently happens in the workplace. Working mothers are often seen as distracted if they speak about their children, while working fathers who do the same are seen as caring and present fathers. It can be argued that the evolution of the workplace is moving backward instead of forward when it comes to finding ways to support working mothers. Women are often overlooked for promotions and leadership roles when they are expecting to have children or already have children. In fact, women will see a 4% decrease in pay per child versus the 6% increase that men will see. Women make up over 50% of the entry-level workforce, but there tends to be a drop-off in middle management, with few women making it to leadership positions. To think, in this day and age, women are afraid to consider having children since it could impact their career trajectory is sad and shows a bigger problem is at play. 

Can We Save Female Leadership?

It’s one thing to understand the problem and another to do something about it. Companies are seeing their female leadership leave to pursue happiness and stability elsewhere. Being overworked and undervalued leads to burnout, which is a key reason many female workers and leaders seek opportunities elsewhere. With motherhood and lack of consideration forcing women to reevaluate their career paths, it’s no wonder many feel ostracized for choosing to be working mothers when it is often used to penalize them. Poor management and development also weigh in on this prominent issue. By providing more flexibility, opportunities to grow, and fair compensation for a job well done, we will see the rate of female leadership grow. It just takes someone to take that first step to ensure a better tomorrow.

We absolutely love this podcast and everything they stand for!

Listen to the Brown Ambition Podcast!

title.rendered: Resolutions to Build a Successful Business this Year

content.rendered:
The start of a new year is the perfect time to take stock of your business and set goals for the coming months. Whether you’re just starting out or have been in business for years, there are always ways to refine, improve and grow. Refining your audience, improving page ranking and learning how to delegate are all effective strategies that can help build a successful business in 2023. In this blog, we will explore how these three areas can be used to help you achieve success this year. So let’s get started on the journey towards building an even better business!

Refining Your Audience

Refining your audience is one of the most important steps to take when developing a successful business. It involves identifying and targeting specific groups of people that are likely to be interested in what you offer. This helps ensure that your marketing efforts will be more effective, resulting in better ROI. 

Things to consider when refining your audience include location, age range, career, and relationship status, to name a few. 

You may have a general idea of who your ideal customer is, but getting more specific can help target the right people, resulting in better conversion rates. 

If you’re just getting started, or need a refresher, check out the Top 5 Branding Mistakes You Want to Avoid. These tips can help you dial in on your target audience.

Improving Page Ranking

Improving page ranking is an integral part of any business’s success. SEO (Search Engine Optimization) and content marketing are two effective strategies that can help businesses achieve a higher page ranking in search results. 

SEO uses keywords to increase visibility and link building to improve a website’s authority. This should be done carefully, as overusing keywords can result in penalties from search engines. Additionally, including meta tags and alt tags within the code of your website will help to make it more easily found. 

Content marketing is the process of creating content that is valuable, relevant, and engaging for readers. Content can be written in the form of blog posts, articles, infographics, videos, or podcasts – all of which are great ways to attract new visitors and keep them coming back for more. To ensure that your content is optimized for search engine rankings, you should include targeted keywords throughout the copy and utilize proper formatting (e.g., headings, lists). Additionally, be sure to include appropriate backlinks within your content to create more internal links that point back to other pages on your website. 

Finally, building relationships with influencers in your industry is another way to improve page rankings. By connecting with influencers online and engaging with them through social media platforms like Twitter, Facebook, or TikTok, you can boost your online presence while establishing yourself as an authority figure in your field of expertise.

By utilizing these three strategies, businesses have a greater chance of achieving higher page rankings in search engine results. This can lead to increased traffic on their website as well as a better overall return on investment for their efforts!

Delegate Tasks and Stop Micromanaging

We know your business is your baby, and you should definitely be attuned to everything that’s going on, but that doesn’t mean you have to do everything yourself. Build a team of people you trust and start to delegate tasks to others. Delegating tasks frees up some of your time, allowing you to focus on other areas of your business. It also lets other people use their skills and knowledge to help your business grow.

Recognizing when you should delegate tasks is a strength. You simply can’t do everything all the time. 

By leveraging the power of SEO optimization, content marketing and relationship-building with influencers in your industry, you can increase page rankings to attract more visitors to your website. Additionally, delegating tasks to others is an effective way to free up time for yourself so that you can focus on important aspects of running a successful business. By following these strategies this year, businesses have a greater chance of achieving success and reaching their goals for 2023! Make sure you take advantage of all the tools available to help grow your business and start setting resolutions today!

title.rendered: 3 Tips to Refresh Your Brand in the New Year

content.rendered:
Branding is important for any business, but it’s especially important in the new year. As we move into 2023, take the time to evaluate your brand to make sure it represents what you want your business to stand for.

Here are three tips to help refresh your brand in the new year.

Refresh your Website

Give your website a new look by updating your content and design!

When it comes to branding, a website is one of the most important pieces of the puzzle. It’s often the first impressions a customer has of your brand and if it’s outdated or difficult to use, it can give a negative first impression. Updating your website is a great way to refresh your brand and make a solid first impression on potential customers and partners or employees.

There are many updates you can do to facelift your website and refresh your brand. One option is to redesign your website’s layout. If your current design is dated or doesn’t reflect your company’s aesthetic, a redesign could be just what you need. Check out templates under your website’s builder. Another option to refresh your site is to update your website’s content to reflect the latest trends and ensure the verbiage, photos and message is relevant to your target audience.

If you’re unsure where to start, there are many online resources that can help. A quick search for “website design tips” or “website refresh ideas” will bring up plenty of helpful articles and tutorials. If you want professional help, you can hire a consultant like us here at Bogues Group to update your website for you.

No matter what route you choose, updating your website is a great way to refresh your brand and make a positive first impression on potential customers.

New Brand Photos

When it comes to your brand, visuals are key. How old are the photos on your site? It might be time for a refresh of your brand photos. Old, outdated shots can make your company look stale and unprofessional. Don’t worry – updating your visuals doesn’t have to be hard. Here are a few simple steps you can take to give your brand an updated look:

1. Choose a new photo style.

If you want to refresh your visuals without changing the overall look and feel of your brand, consider trying a new photo style. This could mean using different filters, angles, or lighting in your shots.

2. Experiment with colors.

Another way to update your visuals is by experimenting with colors. Try using brighter or bolder shades in your branding photos, or mix and match different colors to create an interesting effect.

3. Add text or graphics.

If you really want to make your brand photos pop, consider adding text or graphics to them. This can add an extra layer of interest and help communicate your message more effectively.

4. Use a professional photographer.

If you want high-quality photos that reflect well on your brand, it might be worth hiring a professional photographer. They’ll be able to help you capture the essence of your business and create images that are sure to impress.

Update Your Visual Branding

Updating your visual branding is a great place to start when it comes to refreshing your brand. This can be anything from changing up your logo, to adjusting your color palette, to modernizing your typography. However, it’s important to keep a few things in mind when refreshing your visual branding.

First, make sure any changes you make are true to your brand identity and core values. If you stray too far from what makes your brand unique, you could end up confusing or alienating your audience.

Second, make sure the changes are visually appealing and effective across all mediums. You want your branding to look good on websites, in print materials, on social media posts, and everywhere else it appears.

Finally, be sure to test out the new visuals before making them official. Get feedback from stakeholders, employees, customers and even friends to make sure the changes are well-received. If not, you can always go back to the drawing board!

title.rendered: Women in Business: 3 Traits of Successful Female Leaders

content.rendered:
We recently came across this article by Julia Boorstin about the things she learned while interviewing women for her book, When Women Lead. She shared a few of the top traits she discovered that made women effective and successful business leaders.

One common thread among successful women in business is authenticity. When women are true to themselves, it comes through in everything they do. Women who embrace their strengths and weaknesses and use them to their advantage are those who become the most successful leaders..

Another top trait of successful women is that they rely on data to make hard decisions. These women don’t just go with their gut instinct; they take a step back and look at the facts and figures before making an informed decision. This helps to avoid costly mistakes and ensures that their businesses are run efficiently.

Finally, successful women find purpose in their work. They see their job as more than just a way to make money; they see it as a way to make a difference in the world. This sense of purpose drives these women to achieve great things and helps them stay motivated when times get tough.

Let’s take a deeper look at each of these traits.

Be Authentic to Yourself

Though women have made great strides in the business world over the past few decades, they still face many challenges. One of the biggest obstacles is that they often have to go against their natural character traits in order to be successful leaders.

Many introverted women feel uncomfortable being in the spotlight, and yet they are forced to put on a persona of being assertive and outgoing in order to get ahead. Similarly, many women who are naturally empathetic find it difficult to make tough decisions that may hurt others feelings.
Those who are grateful for what they have can sometimes be too risk-averse when starting or growing their businesses.

On the bright side, these same character traits can actually help women be successful leaders if they learn how to use them correctly.

Julia interviewed Jennifer Holmgren, the CEO of Disruptor 50 company LanzaTech. Boorstin shared that Holmgren is a self-professed introvert who prefers to listen rather than speak, which would generally be a disadvantage to a CEO charged with making changes in her industry. Jennifer managed to make her introversion a superpower. She used her listening skills to figure out what others in negotiation actually wanted and used her empathy for their position to create a compromise that could work for everyone.

Jennifer is a perfect example of using authentic qualities to create a successful business leader.

Rely on Data to Make Tough Decisions

When it comes to being a successful woman in business, humility is key. You have to be willing to put your ego aside and listen to varying opinions if you want to make the best decisions for your company. Relying on data over your initial gut instinct can help you avoid costly mistakes. By looking at the facts and figures, you can make informed decisions that are based on reality rather than personal biases.

Boorstin gave the example of Caryn Seidman, CEO of Clear, pulling the plug on a $24 million marketing plan in 2020 — just before the pandemic hit, and global travel came to a halt. Caryn has used previous and current data to make a solid business decision for her company.

Find Purpose in Your Work, and Focus on It — Especially in Tough Times

Successful women in business often find purpose in their work. These women see their job as more than just a way to make money; they see it as a way to make a difference in the world. This sense of purpose drives them to achieve great things and helps them stay motivated when times get tough.

If you want to be a successful leader in business, you need to find purpose in the work you do. Ask yourself why you started your business in the first place and what you hope to achieve. Once you have a clear goal in mind, focus on achieving it, even if it takes baby steps. Success is not a one-time event; it’s something you have to work for every day. The most successful women keep their goals in sight, celebrate milestone wins big and small, and adjust their course as necessary.

These traits truly define some of the most successful business women we know. We hope you can apply these tips to your own endeavors!

title.rendered: Why Giving Tuesday Matters for Businesses

content.rendered:
In today’s competitive business landscape, it’s more important than ever for companies to give back to their communities. Giving Tuesday provides businesses with an opportunity to do just that! On Giving Tuesday, companies can make donations to charities and causes that are important to them, volunteer their time or services, or promote philanthropy among their employees. Social media can be a powerful tool for spreading awareness about Giving Tuesday and encouraging others to get involved.

What is Giving Tuesday, and why should businesses get involved

Giving Tuesday is a global day of giving that falls on the Tuesday following Thanksgiving (in the United States). The day is dedicated to giving back to charities and causes that are important to individuals and businesses. There are many different ways companies and individuals can get involved with Giving Tuesday – from making donations to volunteering time or services.

There are several reasons for businesses to get involved with Giving Tuesday. First, it provides businesses with an opportunity to give back to their community. By supporting charities and causes that are important to them, businesses can help make their community a better place. Second, Giving Tuesday helps promote philanthropy among employees. When businesses get involved with Giving Tuesday, they can encourage their employees to participate in charitable activities such as donating time or money. It also demonstrates that the business cares about the communities its employees are part of. Finally, Giving Tuesday provides a great opportunity for marketing and branding. By getting involved with Giving Tuesday, businesses can raise awareness about their company and its philanthropic initiatives.

How can businesses get involved with Giving Tuesday?

Here are a few examples of how your business can get involved:

1. Make a donation to a charity or cause that is important to you.

2. Volunteer your time or services to a local charity or cause.

3. Promote philanthropy among your employees.

4. Raise awareness about Giving Tuesday on social media.

5. Host a fundraising event for a local charity or cause

How can social media be used to promote Giving Tuesday

One of the best ways to promote Giving Tuesday is to use social media. Social media can be used to raise awareness about and encourage others to get involved. Here are a few ways businesses can use social media to promote Giving Tuesday:

1. Share information about Giving Tuesday on your social media channels.

2. Encourage your employees to share information about Giving Tuesday on their social media channels.

3. Host a contest or giveaway on your social media channels to raise awareness and encourage donations.

4. Highlight the charities and causes that you are supporting on Giving Tuesday on your social media channels.

5. Post photos and videos of your employees volunteering or making donations on your social media channels.

Participating in Giving Tuesday as an individual or company can be a great way to raise spirits and morale. Uplifting the communities we live in helps strengthen bonds that are vital to personal and professional success. It’s also a great way to get your brand in the public eye with a positive connotation.

title.rendered: 3 Top PR Challenges (And how to Overcome them)

content.rendered:
The world of public relations can be confusing at times. For someone that is not familiar with the function of public relations they can sometimes find it impossible to understand how to measure the impact of the campaign. The first step is deciding the goal of the campaign and desired outcome you want your audience to take away. Once that is determined, a PR Professional can assist with creating a strategic plan including specific measurable tactics to achieve the attended benchmarks. If you aren’t able to hire a PR PRO just yet, don’t worry. We have you covered. Here are some of the top 3 challenges of public relations and how to overcome them.

PR’s Biggest Challenges

1. Measuring the ROI of PR campaigns
2. Connecting with relevant media and influencers
3. Listening to online conversations.

For years, in the communications industry, the worlds of public relations and marketing have remained separate. In today’s age the line between the two disciplines are far more blurred and truly work hand and hand. The departments need to and should be merged. Public relations combined with marketing efforts helps overcome the age old question of how do you measure the ROI of a PR campaign. “They are having to work together as, ultimately, what they do drives the same result, whether it be a spike in sales, stock price (in the case of a publicly traded company) or market share. And today it is possible for both parties to directly link their work to it.” Marketing has a history of tracking key metrics in several different ways to show value and impact. The next important step after deciding on your goal is research.

Research is the foundation and cornerstone of all of work in the PR world. This research includes trends, statistics, media outlets and influencers. Research is also how you connect with the correct media outlets and influencers. By doing your due diligence and finding a commonality, you can connect authentically with influencers and media outlets by sharing stories they will find relevant. Journalists and reporters may not open or respond to every email but they will notice and reward those who take the time to do their research.

Listening to online conversations can make or break your campaign – but it can be challenging if you don’t know where to start. Utilizing technology or softwares like Google Alerts, Hootsuite and Tweetdeck are just a few free tools that keep you in the know whenever your client is mentioned. Listening and observing as a thought leader and when to share those thoughts is a key skill of PR success. “Share of voice is one of the metrics that is key to determining the effectiveness of what we do in PR,” agrees Mardiks. “Clients want to drive and lead conversations that are important to their business and brands. It is a key way of determining if we’re being successful.”

There is no doubt that public relations is vital to gain awareness, sales and build trust with your audience. It can be challenging but when you get that big media hit, it makes it all worth it. For more PR and marketing tips join our newsletter by clicking here.

title.rendered: Top 5 Branding Mistakes You Want to Avoid

content.rendered:
Your brand is how your company appears to consumers. It involves the tone of your copy (informational, conversational, etc.) and the visual imagery you put out. Marketing your brand establishes and grows a relationship between your company and consumers. Brand marketing highlights the entirety of the brand, instead of an individual product or service.

There are a lot of moving parts when it comes to building a brand, and it can be easy to get off on the wrong foot. Here are 5 branding mistakes you want to avoid when starting off.

Writing Bad Copy

Your copy or text is the tool you use to persuade consumers to care about, and ultimately use you and/or your product. Hook your audience with a good graphic, but engage them with amazing copy!

Establish a brand voice that you will use to speak to your audience through your copy. Will you be informational, casual, or somewhere in between?

Inconsistency

Consistency refers to a few different things across your brand.

First, be consistent in your brand voice and keep the same general tone across your copy. Inconsistency in your copy can cause confusion when it comes to your brand’s image.

Second, post regularly! Keeping a posting schedule helps keep your brand in people’s line of sight, allowing them to become familiar with your brand.

Colors and logos should stay consistent, too! This helps people instantly/quickly recognize your company.

Relying on Trends

Trends are great for fun and quick content, but they shouldn’t be the bread and butter of your feed.

Establish a brand foundation while using trends for extra content and to elicit engagement.

Not Identifying Your Audience

You have this great idea for a product or service, but who is it ultimately for?

You have to know who your audience is in order to effectively market to them.
Where are they?
How old are they?
What do they do?
What do they need?
Why do they need you?!

These are things you should think about when building the foundation of your brand and creating content to get your name out there. You want your image to land in the right places!

Not Knowing When to Get Help!

Not everyone has the inherent know-how when it comes to branding, and that’s okay!

You can get branding guidance from people who have done the legwork of understanding branding and marketing. This help can range anywhere from a simple consultation to get you headed in the right direction or to completely off-loading your brand work. The great part about off-loading tasks within your business is that you free up time and energy to put into other ideas.

Don’t be afraid to seek help when you need it!

title.rendered: 3 Ways Businesses Can Use Events to Recruit Top Talent

content.rendered:
No matter how you look at it, the pandemic changed our way of living forever. It’s had a significant impact on the way we work. It showed senior leaders we actually can get things done without a “butts in seats” philosophy and introduced us to a true hybrid lifestyle between virtual (or digital) and IRL (in real life). 

COVID triggered an unprecedented churn in the job market. As we look to 2023, some companies are still reeling from the sting of the great resignation of 2020. The nation’s “quit rate” reached a 20-year high last November. A new Pew Research Center survey finds that low pay, a lack of opportunities for advancement, and feeling disrespected at work are among the top reasons Americans quit their jobs last year. The survey also finds that those who quit and are now employed elsewhere are more likely than not to say their current job has better pay, more opportunities for advancement, and more work-life balance and flexibility.

From working with our clients, Jaclynn, Managing Partner, says, “Manpower is one of the top pain points. With headcounts shrinking and responsibilities increasing, now more than ever, it’s time to get creative with recruiting and retention.” In-person events are back and remain one of the most effective ways to recruit top-tier talent. 

Here are 3 Innovative Recruiting Event Examples that blew us out of the water and got BIG RESULTS!

 

AMA (Ask Me Anything) Sessions 

Ask Me Anything Sessions have become quite popular in the world of recruiting. These informal virtual sessions with the CEO or other senior leaders offer transparency and a look into the company culture. 

As a best practice, your AMA should zero-in on a specific topic. For example, if you have a high volume of applicants interested in a particular role, ask a recruiter to moderate a session with the hiring manager to field questions about the interview process, hiring timelines, benefits, and team culture

 Pro tip: come prepared with a list of FAQs to help get the conversation going in case the conversation slows down.

To get some ideas of what this looks like in action, watch this AMA with Nestlé USA’s CEO Steve Presley: Ask Me Anything: Nestlé USA CEO Steve Presley

Key takeaways:

  • AMAs are a great engagement opportunity
  • Pick the right moderator and subject matter expert (SME) or leader
  • AMAs can be used for internal and external audiences

 

NBA Hackathon

 

Sports aren’t all about athleticism. Hackathons present a unique type of sport that focuses on mental strength rather than physical and requires a computer, not a basketball. For two years, the NBA hosted a hackathon to attract college students to contribute to developing analytical tools to overcome the challenges in the NBA. Teams work for 24 hours before they present their work to a panel of judges, NBA personnel, and the media. The grand prize includes lunch with NBA commissioner Adam Silver, and a trip to the NBA All-Star Game.

Hackathons are a fantastic way to predict how a candidate will perform by having them complete a task before hiring. These types of competitions have evolved from a way for a company to interactively showcase a product to the public to an effective recruitment campaign.

Key Takeaways

  • Hackathons showcase the potential of candidates.
  • Participants find solutions to your business problems.
  • An attractive prize can help pull in participants.

 

LEGO Brick Factor

 

The LEGO Brick Factor is a national competition held by LEGO of 100 competitors, tasked with completing three building challenges to earn the title of Master Model Builder at a Legoland Discovery Center. Winners are hired on the spot!

The challenges ask the builders to create pieces based on prompts such as “build something from your favorite book.” There’s no better way to see if a candidate can be successful at a job than hosting an event where they can prove just that!

Key Takeaways:

  • Competitions can find hidden talent.
  • Events not only attract new talent. They can be a fun event for the public, that boosts brand awareness.
  • Giving candidates tasks they would need to complete in an actual work environment is a great way to test compatibility and capability

title.rendered: 3 Lessons Entrepreneurs Can Learn from Steph Curry

content.rendered:
As I sat in the crowd anxiously awaiting the ceremony and fondly recounted my first love, I was a bit confused: who graduates in August?

Today, 3-pointers have almost become synonymous with Steph Curry or the ‘Babyface Assassin’. Steph’s family and mine grew up and attended schools together, his famous dad donned a Barney costume for my brother’s birthday. We spent  countless hours together: from family vacations to hanging at the Hornets games, we’ve created many cherished memories together. Vowing to continue the 100% student-athlete graduation rate under the tenure of his coach, Steph – after 11 years in the league – went back to get his degree. Being present to witness the conferring of his degree, retiring of his number, and induction into the Davidson College Hall of Fame was a full circle moment. As a lifelong friend, this was nothing short of inspirational. As an entrepreneur, it quickly made sense why we were all there.

Steph’s body of work extends beyond the court and includes a diverse business portfolio consisting of television projects, foundation work and tech investments. I truly felt as if we just witnessed a one-man commencement ceremony. An epic and fitting honor for a special guy. Steph formed SC30 in 2017 to manage his investments, brand partnerships and philanthropic ventures. He also has a production company, Unanimous Media, which has a multi-year development deal with Sony Pictures. In 2018, the NBA star invested $37 million into the esports organization TSM that was valued at a whopping $410 million just two years later. His tenacity, business acumen and humility are just a handful of reasons why entrepreneurs can learn a few lessons from the iconic shooting guard and serial entrepreneur.

Lesson 1: Be yourself. “Be the best version of yourself in anything you do. You don’t have to live anybody else’s story.”

Reading Steph’s scouting report as a youngster, a future in the NBA, let alone becoming an All Star and three-time NBA Champion was far from a given for the unranked, under-the-radar sharp-shooter. Steph was seen by many of the major universities as “The Underdog” and was often overlooked. He stayed the course and it worked out in his favor. This is similar for entrepreneurs and small business owners: recognizing your unique selling position and remaining true to your authentic story will separate you from your competitors even in a crowded market.

Lesson 2: Stay focused on the long-term goal not the short-term gain. “Success is not an accident, success is actually a choice.”

Steph knew when we were kids that he wanted to play in the League despite not being highly recruited. He knew if he consistently put in the work it would pay off. He implemented routines and trained himself at the age of 14 how to improve his shot and worked hard to inspire those around him. Growing a business, there will be times of intense highs, which should be celebrated but there will also be growing pains. Remember to stay focused and grounded, prepare for the rainy days and always celebrate the wins. In basketball and in business (even the business of basketball), realizing the power of automation and delegation coupled with unwavering trusting in your team will lead to true success.

Lesson 3: Faith over Fear. “I’ve never been afraid of big moments. I get butterflies. I get nervous and anxious, but I think those are good signs that I am ready for the moment.”

Let’s face it, being an entrepreneur is rewarding but it is hard work and it isn’t for everyone. If you find yourself scratching the itch, and can cultivate passion, drive and success, then get after it! Even your favorite NBA All Star gets butterflies but how you harness that energy is what makes a champion.

title.rendered: Top Traits of an Impactful Leader

content.rendered:
Some people are natural born leaders while others happen to become leaders by circumstance, education, or experience. Good leadership and leading organizations know how to work with others and have a gift that can be shared and learned from. A strong leader knows how to digest loads of information and transform it so that others can understand the same information but in a clear and concise manner. Employees and contractors want to feel heard, respected and appreciated. It takes a leadership mentality skill set to be able to identify what your team needs, then how to properly execute and implement those needs. Check out a few top traits to adopt when in a leadership position:

  1. Effective listening goes a long way. People want and need to be heard to feel understood.
  2. Exhibit Empathy. Everyone is human and is being pulled in many directions at one time, both in their jobs and at home. Even acknowledging this will help to close communication gaps.
  3. Setting clear goals and expectations is key. Everyone works differently.
  4. Hold yourself accountable and be responsible. Leaders can be under a lot of pressure to produce and perform at all times. Everyone can make a mistake or say something they regret. Hold yourself accountable and acknowledge if you yourself have a bad day!

Leaders are important because they help to communicate the vision and mission of an organization or its employees and/or clients. Leaders can help to provide direction and use their experiences to increase the productivity and communication in an organization.

title.rendered: Freelancers and Side Hustlers: Top 5 Personal Branding Must Dos to Earn More

content.rendered:
The existing job market and changes in the workforce are causing workers to gravitate toward freelancing or even picking up a side hustle in addition to their career. 45% of working Americans report having a side hustle1. That amounts to roughly 70 million people. Among millennials, that statistic rises to 50%2. With this growing trend it is vital for your brand to stand out and here’s how to do that:

1. Build a landing page or website/portfolio
There are several platforms to help you host your website or portfolio. They range from free to expensive and are mostly user friendly. Some platforms do not require any coding experience which will make you look more experienced. Some of our favorite website tools and platforms can be found on the downloadable resource list.

2. Maintain a steady social media presence
Social media is a direct outlet to your audience and a way to highlight your personal brand. Using social, you can plan ahead by creating batch content and to stay ahead of schedule. Be sure to use one of the helpful scheduling tools to keep your content consistent while freeing up time.

3. Emphasize your unique traits/skills
Everyone is unique and has their own special skills so take stock of your uniqueness and how it applies to your brand. Find ways to emphasize yourself to your audience.

4. Identify and understand your audience
One of the most important questions you need to ask yourself is: who is my brand for? Who am I trying to relate or connect with? How do they get their information? Doing research to identify what group or demographic you appeal to helps to determine your audience.

5. A system for maintaining your projects/workload
Competing to-dos and tasks are hard to keep up with and prioritize. As a business owner, the tasks can pile up between your role with your company, client work and prospecting all while maintaining a personal life. Thankfully there are several softwares and apps to keep your team and yourself in check. Softwares vary from simple formats like the To Do list app which is a simple digital task list to more robust like Asana where you are able to assign, track and analyze all company wide tasks. Choosing the right software is key for your success.

Successful personal branding relies heavily on consistency, organization and creativity. Once you have clearly identified your unique skills and traits you can begin creating your brand. When choosing your colors, fonts and taglines, back your choices up with research and life experiences. Trust your gut and go after it – if you still need guidance, we got your back.
